publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — one MORE line in Monday's Telegram digest, and one admin API that was never reachable is gone. THE FINDING: `weeklyReport.generate` was registered in the tRPC tree (routers.ts:153) and had ZERO callers — `grep -rn weeklyReport client/` returns nothing, no cron references it, and the only other hits were the router's own file plus two test fixtures listing its name. `notifyWeeklyReport` in email-notify.ts was identically dead: the sole reference was auto-invoice.test.ts asserting `typeof === 'function'` — a test that proved the export existed and nothing more. So a 'weekly intelligence report' existed in code, was documented, was permission-checked, and had never once run.  WHY THIS IS A COLLAPSE, NOT A DELETION. The tempting read is 'nobody clicked it, nobody wants it'. The evidence says otherwise: it required clicking, and this operator consumes pushed reports (daily SMS, Telegram digests) and no pull-only ones. What went unused was the TRANSPORT, not the content — the same finding that made the revenue digest a push in #1427. So its content moves to the live pushed job: `Demand: N leads · N bookings · N callbacks (N still open)`, where unworked callbacks are the actionable half.  ★ A CONSISTENCY TRAP CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED. The obvious implementation is `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leads`. That would have made this report DISAGREE with the daily one: dailyReport.ts:48 counts leads through `countActionableLeads` (shared/leadSource.ts), which excludes a `source='callback'` lead carrying a `callbackId` because that row and its callback_requests row are the SAME PERSON. A raw count double-counts them. Re-expressing that predicate in SQL would have forked a definition the repo deliberately centralized, so the digest fetches the rows and calls the shared function — one definition, no drift. A test pins it: a 4-row lead fixture containing exactly one callback-linked duplicate must yield 3, and the comment says out loud that a reading of 4 means someone re-implemented the rule in SQL.  EVIDENCE: weeklyRevenueDigest.test.ts now 16 tests (3 new: the shared-rule lead count, the demand line, and the open-callbacks callout suppressed at zero). Serial run of the three touched files: 3 files / 68 tests passed, exit 0. tsc --noEmit exit 0 WITH the router deleted — the compiler confirms nothing referenced it. validate:routes ✓ ('every App.tsx route is registered'). lint:source ✓.  NOT CLAIMED: the digest has still never fired in production — first firing is Monday 2026-08-10 business hours ET, and the demand line is asserted against fixtures, not a live send. No admin UI changed, because the deleted procedure had no UI to change.

WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES — nothing on Instagram, which is how this was found. The operator asked why autonomous reels had stopped; production said the rest.  ★ ONE — A BILLING WALL FILED AS A TRANSIENT BLIP. Reel job #1380001 (2026-08-04 18:03, cron) failed with Higgsfield's grace_daily_limit_reached / unlock_full_access_notice. That text matched NONE of the eight classifier patterns — no "billing", no "exhausted", and no "rate" for RATE_LIMIT — so it fell through to UNKNOWN, whose policy is RETRY_BACKOFF and whose operator-facing reason literally reads "unrecognised failure - treated as transient, but review the message". The daily cron re-attempted every day and NOTHING alerted. It now classifies as QUOTA_OR_CREDIT -> PAUSE_PROVIDER, which stops the lane and raises a human.  Deliberately NOT RATE_LIMIT, and the difference is money: RATE_LIMIT is RETRY_WITHOUT_CONSUMING_ATTEMPT, built for a request refused before work began that clears on its own. A grace-tier daily cap does not clear by waiting and cannot be retried out of - it needs a plan upgrade. A test asserts it is not that class.  ★ THE TEST CAUGHT A TRAP IN MY OWN FIX. The first draft appended the new wordings to the existing QUOTA_OR_CREDIT regex, which is wrapped in  ... . `_` is a WORD character, so   never fires inside an underscore-joined token:  grace[_ ]daily[_ ]limit  does NOT match "grace_daily_limit_reached", because the boundary it wants sits between `limit` and `_reached` with word characters on both sides. Three cases went red. The plan-wall patterns are now their own entry and the working credit regex is untouched.  ★ TWO — A TRUNCATED RESPONSE REPORTED AS A BACKTICK. ig_autopost_log carried `Unexpected token '`', "```json
{"... is not valid JSON` (2026-08-05) and `Unterminated string in JSON at position 830` (2026-08-01). Both are ONE root cause - the model's output was cut off mid-object - and neither message says so; the first names the backtick, which is the only detail that does not matter. parseJsonObject now detects an opening brace with no closing one and throws `LLM response truncated before the JSON object closed (N chars received) - raise max_tokens for this call`, and wraps genuine syntax errors instead of leaking the raw parser text into a column the operator reads.  ★ AND A MUTATION PROVED PART OF MY OWN FIX DEAD. The draft also stripped an UNCLOSED fence. Disabling that line changed no behaviour: the brace isolation already recovers the object whenever one closed, and when none closed the truncation branch fires first either way. It was removed rather than kept with a comment claiming it fixed the prod error. The surviving branch is verified load-bearing - disabling it turns 2 cases red.  EVIDENCE: server/providerErrorAndLlmJsonTruth.test.ts (10), built from the EXACT prod stderr payload rather than a paraphrase, MUTATION-VERIFIED FOUR WAYS - removing the plan-wall pattern (3 red) · reclassifying it as RATE_LIMIT (4 red) · disabling the truncation branch (2 red) · deleting the truncation message (1 red). One further mutation SURVIVED and that is why a line was deleted; the first attempt at it silently failed to apply and reported a false pass, so the applied ones are proven by echoing the removed text and by git diff --stat. A regression case pins that the other six error classes are unchanged. Full serial suite: 405 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,981 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0. tsc --noEmit clean.  NOT CLAIMED: neither fix makes a reel. The Higgsfield account is behind a plan-tier daily cap - an operator billing action - and this change only makes that state stop the lane loudly instead of retrying it silently. No production run has exercised either path since the change; the classification is asserted against the recorded payload, not against a new live failure.

capability-ledger-updated.ref: docs/operations/capability-ledger.json IS part of this diff - template-stock-reel-lane is edited rather than deferred, because the lane genuinely gains a second reachable entry point and pretending otherwise would understate the change. What was added: a tests entry for server/reelFreeLaneFallback.test.ts (15), and a deploymentId amendment recording that the new entry point is ALSO not deployed. NO STATE MOVES. operationalState stays where it was and all three blockers stand unedited - in particular the P2 'verified locally, never in production' and the P2 'no reel produced by this lane has ever been PUBLISHED, so whether the format earns reach is unmeasured'. That is the honest reading: the fallback is gated behind REEL_FALLBACK_TO_TEMPLATE_STOCK, which is unset in production, so nothing prod DOES changed on merge. Claiming a state gain on the strength of an unset flag is exactly the unearned claim this ledger exists to prevent. Checked rather than assumed: grep over capability-ledger.json confirms template-stock-reel-lane is the only entry describing this lane; no other capability entry mentions reelPipeline's provider selection or the beat loop.

render-spend-trajectory.ref: THIS DIFF CHANGES SPEND, and the change is downward and bounded. The rule fires on server/services/reelPipeline.ts, which is where render spend is both reserved and settled, so here is the whole trajectory.  BEFORE: a paid provider returning a verdict no retry can clear (QUOTA_OR_CREDIT, AUTH_INVALID -> PAUSE_PROVIDER) sent the job terminal. Spend for the remaining beats: zero, because nothing rendered - and no reel either. AFTER, and only when REEL_FALLBACK_TO_TEMPLATE_STOCK=true: the remaining beats render on the local ffmpeg lane. Spend for those beats is still zero (reelClipCostUsd('template_stock') is 0 and the lane makes no provider call - templateStockStudio.ts contains exactly one fetch, a download of an already-hosted hero image), and now there IS a reel. No path in this diff can increase spend: the flip is one-way and only ever moves from a paid lane to the free one, never the reverse.  ★ THE REAL FINDING, and it is a defect this change would otherwise have INTRODUCED. Settlement read `clipUrls.length * reelClipCostUsd(videoProvider)`, and the comment directly above it warns that settling at a flat rate is 'what made a mid-flight provider flip undetectable in the ledger, and would settle a free local reel as if it had spent Seedance money'. Introducing a mid-job flip made videoProvider stop being the provider that actually rendered, so a degraded reel would have billed every clip at the paid rate - resurrecting the exact bug already fixed once on the repair lane (#1343, where a hardcoded seedance1_5 filed template_stock repairs under Higgsfield's name). The reserve() call at enqueue anticipates this in writing: 'a mid-flight provider flip can still diverge - settlement is where actuals must be reconciled.' Settlement now splits the bill: paidClips * reelClipCostUsd(videoProvider) + freeLaneClips * reelClipCostUsd('template_stock'), where freeLaneClips counts what the free lane actually rendered this run. With no flip freeLaneClips is 0 and the expression is arithmetically identical to the original, so unflipped jobs settle exactly as before.  The reservation itself is UNTOUCHED: still created at enqueue against the selected provider at beatsCount * reelClipCostUsd(reservedProvider), still checked against the daily ceiling. A degraded job therefore over-reserves and under-settles, which is the conservative direction and the same direction any partially-failed job already takes.  EVIDENCE: server/reelFreeLaneFallback.test.ts (15), MUTATION-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS - dropping the durable-storage assert on the flip (2 red), dropping the opt-in flag gate (2 red), broadening the predicate from PAUSE_PROVIDER to any error (3 red), dropping the beat re-run (2 red), and reverting settlement to flat per-clip billing (1 red). Each mutation script fails loudly if its anchor is absent, because a mutation that does not apply looks exactly like a passing test; the source file was restored byte-identical after every run (sha256 compared, identical=True both times).  Suites: 18 files / 192 passed across every suite importing reelPipeline or socialPipeline. tsc --noEmit clean. Full nickstire pre-commit gate green (routes, hooks, source lint, brand voice, tsc).  NOT CLAIMED: no production run, no live provider call, and no measurement against generation_reservations. The flag is unset in prod, so on merge this diff changes nothing that runs. The free lane has still never published a reel - that P2 blocker stands.
